title: Sex representation in trials relative to indication-specific disease burden in FDA-approved drugs (2015–2023)
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74469-z

Analysis of clinical trial cohorts for 218 FDA-approved drugs finds that, although women are now often adequately represented in trials, progress has plateaued and gaps persist in specific disease areas; the study outlines actionable next steps.

title: Optimal dismantling of directed networks
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74467-1

Dismantling directed networks is critical for controlling complex systems. Here, authors introduce TAD, a trophic analysis-based method that efficiently fragments networks by targeting nodes with high network incoherence centrality.

title: Framework-templated gas lattices in metal-organic frameworks
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74776-5

Researchers show that metal-organic frameworks can organize confined gases into ordered lattice-like states, opening new ways to control adsorption and gas transport in porous materials.

title: MiT fusions, TSC1–TSC2 divergence, and stem-like programs reveal distinct origins and vulnerabilities in PEComa
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74545-4

Perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasms are rare tumors with limited molecular stratification to guide treatment. Here, authors identify recurrent MITF gene fusions and four molecular subtypes linked to prognosis and therapy response, including an aggressive stem-like group with potential sensitivity to immunotherapy.

title: Global current systems in the magnetosphere of Mercury
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74847-7

Mercury’s magnetic environment is shaped by electric currents driven by the solar wind. Here, the authors show a global map of these currents, revealing equatorial ring currents and a previously unknown current around Mercury’s north pole.

title: Cluster replicability in single-cell and single-nucleus atlases of the mouse brain
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74171-0

Large mouse brain cell atlases are foundational resources, but their reproducibility is unclear. Here, the authors compare two major atlases, find 2,009 matching cell clusters (~40%), and reveal limits of marker genes and fine-scale annotation.

title: Jumbo circular extrachromosomal elements of methane-oxidizing archaea with variably extensive metabolic and defense gene repertoires
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74423-z

Archaeal extrachromosomal elements are poorly understood. Here, Shi et al. identify large, circular extrachromosomal elements associated with anaerobic methane-oxidizing archaea, encoding metabolic enzymes and defense systems.

title: Electrochemical selective oxygen transfer enables energy-efficient environmental deoxygenation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74367-4

This study reports an electrochemical system that selectively removes oxygen from storage environments, reducing energy use in low-oxygen preservation while maintaining produce quality and supporting lower-carbon cold-chain logistics.
